verdict: Biogen's revenue grew 11% to $2.8B as its growth portfolio jumped 49%, but $284M of acquired research charges plus deal and restructuring costs pushed it to a small $21M GAAP loss.

segments.name: Multiple sclerosis products
segments.note: Tecfidera, Vumerity, Avonex, Plegridy and Tysabri — the legacy franchise, down 13% as older drugs lose ground.

segments.name: Rare disease products
segments.note: Spinraza, Skyclarys and Qalsody — up 27%, led by Spinraza's move to a high-dose regimen.

segments.name: Specialized immunology products
segments.note: Empaveli and Syfovre, added with the Apellis acquisition that closed in May 2026 — a new revenue line this year.

segments.name: Biosimilars
segments.note: Copycat versions of other companies' biologics — down 16%.

segments.name: Other products
segments.note: Zurzuvae, the postpartum-depression pill — up 53% on strong demand.

segments.name: Anti-CD20 therapeutic programs
segments.note: Royalties and profit share from Ocrevus and other anti-CD20 drugs sold by partners — up 1%, high-margin income with no product sales.

segments.name: Alzheimer's collaboration
segments.note: Biogen's 50% share of the Leqembi collaboration with Eisai — up 60%.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing, royalty and other
segments.note: Making drugs for others plus royalties — flat YoY.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Clinical trials and drug development — up 32% on trials for felzartamab, salanersen and litifilimab, plus Apellis's costs.

opex.name: Acquired in-process R&D and milestones
opex.note: Paying for research bought from others — mainly the RayThera acquisition — expensed immediately because the projects are not yet approved drugs.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling the medicines and running the company — up 26%, including Apellis's commercial operations.

opex.name: Amortization and impairment of acquired intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down drug rights bought in the Apellis and Reata acquisitions over time.

opex.name: Collaboration sharing, restructuring and other
opex.note: Sharing Leqembi collaboration profits with Eisai ($78M), Fit for Growth restructuring charges ($67M), and revaluing future acquisition payments (under $1M this quarter).

otherDetail: Other (income) expense, net was a $137M expense in the quarter. Biogen reports no separate operating-income line; the operating step shown is total revenue less every reported cost except that line.
oneTimers: $284M of acquired in-process R&D, upfront and milestone expense, primarily tied to the RayThera acquisition — the main reason GAAP EPS was -$0.14 while non-GAAP EPS was $2.62.
$67M of restructuring charges and $173M of amortization and impairment of acquired intangible assets, from the Apellis and Reata deals, also weighed on GAAP results.

takeaways.title: The growth portfolio is taking over
takeaways.text: Growth Portfolio revenue reached $1.26B, up 49%, and is now 63% of core pharmaceutical revenue — including the first full quarter from the acquired Apellis products Syfovre ($191M) and Empaveli ($52M).

takeaways.title: A deal charge caused the loss
takeaways.text: Acquired research expense of $284M, mainly for RayThera, plus $67M of restructuring, turned a profitable operating business into a $21M GAAP net loss. Non-GAAP EPS, which excludes these items, was $2.62.

takeaways.title: The old MS franchise keeps shrinking
takeaways.text: Multiple sclerosis product revenue fell 13% to $919M. Biogen's story now depends on growth products — Spinraza (+23%), Leqembi (+67%) and Skyclarys (+34%) — outgrowing that decline.

footerNote: MS revenue is shown $1M higher ($920M vs the reported $919M) so categories sum exactly to reported revenue of $2,804M.
